The top-5 features shift substantially: \texttt{surp\_range}, \texttt{surp\_pos\_corr}, \texttt{prob\_std}, \texttt{surp\_half\_diff}, and \texttt{surp\_std} replace the perplexity tail statistics (\texttt{p90\_ppl}, \texttt{var\_surprisal}) that dominate in base models.
This feature shift suggests instruction tuning compresses the perplexity distribution (reducing tail discriminability) while preserving positional and range-based surprisal patterns.

Two caveats apply: (1) self-reference evaluation may inflate or deflate accuracy relative to cross-reference evaluation (cf.\ \S\ref{app:ref_ablation}); (2) a single instruction-tuned model does not establish the generality of the feature shift across architectures or instruction-tuning recipes.

\label{app:downstream}

We fine-tune Pythia-410M with LoRA ($r{=}16$, $\alpha{=}32$) on depth-stratified subsets (500 samples each) and evaluate held-out perplexity (200 samples, 50 per depth).

\paragraph{Cross-domain transfer.}
All prior experiments use WikiText-103 as the seed corpus.
To test domain dependence, we repeat the pipeline with arXiv abstracts as the seed text (Pythia-1.4B, nucleus $p{=}0.95$, 500 samples per depth, d0--d3).
Five-fold cross-validation yields 74.1\% $\pm$ 2.0\% accuracy, compared to ${\sim}$78\% on the WikiText seed.
Per-depth F1 shows the familiar pattern: d0 = 1.00, d1 = 0.78, d2 = 0.52, d3 = 0.66, with d2 remaining the most challenging class.
The 4pp accuracy gap relative to WikiText likely reflects the narrower stylistic range of scientific abstracts, which may reduce the distributional contrast between adjacent depths.
These results provide preliminary evidence that the perplexity-based features capture properties of the recursive generation process rather than domain-specific artifacts of the seed corpus.

\subsection{Cross-Seed Replication}
\label{app:seed_replication}

Table~\ref{tab:seed_replication} reports within-seed accuracy for all three model families (nucleus, depths 0--3) under two independent LoRA training seeds.

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\small
\caption{Cross-seed replication (nucleus $p{=}0.95$, d0--d3). seed=42 is the primary benchmark (matching Table~\ref{tab:main_matrix}); seed=43 is an independent replication.}
\label{tab:seed_replication}
\begin{tabular}{@{}llccc@{}}
\toprule
Model & Seed & Acc (\%) & 95\% CI & $\Delta$ (pp) \\
\midrule
Pythia-1.4B & 42 & 78.70 & [78.10, 79.24] & --- \\
Pythia-1.4B & 43 & 78.84 & [78.13, 79.52] & $+$0.14 \\
\midrule
OLMo-1B & 42 & 78.94 & [78.38, 79.48] & --- \\
OLMo-1B & 43 & 82.11 & [81.77, 82.54] & $+$3.17 \\
\midrule
GPT-2~XL & 42 & 84.28 & [83.78, 84.80] & --- \\
GPT-2~XL & 43 & 86.32 & [86.17, 86.49] & $+$2.04 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

Seed=43 yields higher accuracy in all three models ($+$0.14 to $+$3.17\,pp, same direction).
For Pythia ($+$0.14\,pp), CIs overlap, consistent with noise; for OLMo ($+$3.17\,pp) and GPT-2~XL ($+$2.04\,pp), CIs do not overlap, so LoRA initialization has a non-trivial effect on absolute accuracy (${\sim}$1--3\,pp).
Top-3 features are identical across all seeds and models (\texttt{p90\_ppl}, \texttt{var\_surprisal}, \texttt{p75\_ppl}); depth ordering is preserved in every configuration.

\paragraph{Outlier handling.}
Feature extraction occasionally produces extreme perplexity values (outlier passages); we apply per-feature clipping at $\pm 10^{10}$ before classification, affecting ${<}0.1$\% of samples.

论文贡献定位为 "task formalization + systematic empirical study"，classifier 是标准 RF。§1 坦诚说 "contribution centers on task formalization...rather than algorithmic novelty"，但 EMNLP 审稿人对 "RF on features" 的接受度因人而异。

2. Introduction 中引用 HELM/MMLU/MAGE 作为 benchmark/analysis paper 先例（1 句话）。

### M2. 尺度泛化弱 [风险: HIGH]

14B cross-ref: 44.1%（4 类 chance=25%, 仅 1.76× chance）。现代 LLM 主流 70B+，1–1.5B 结果的实际部署价值有限。

Single-feature regression on mean perplexity performs at chance (25.1\%); zero-shot LLMs (best 36.2\%; Appendix~\ref{app:zeroshot_prompt}) also fail; depth signal resides in distributional statistics inaccessible from surface text.

1	\section*{Limitations}
2	\label{sec:limitations}
3	
4	\paragraph{Full-replacement vs.\ accumulation.}
5	The primary benchmark uses full-replacement chains; real-world contamination involves accumulation at unknown mixing ratios \cite{gerstgrasser2024_accumulate}.
6	At 25--50\% synthetic mixing, accuracy drops 8--15\,pp and $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}3$ is preserved in 5/6 tested cells (GPT-2~XL nucleus at 50\% drops to $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}2$; d2v3 AUC\,=\,0.695, marginally below threshold; Table~\ref{tab:accum_auc}); extension to larger models and higher ratios remains future work.
7	
8	\paragraph{Scale and generalization boundaries.}
9	At 14B, cross-reference accuracy drops to 44.1\% ($\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}2$), with reference-model mismatch accounting for ${\sim}$7\,pp; cross-strategy transfer (d1--d3: 45.9\%) and web-crawl false positive rates (15--34\% base rate across C4, FineWeb, and RedPajama) are partially resolved by confidence thresholding ($T{=}0.10$ reduces FPR to 0.1--7\%) but not fully eliminated.
10	
11	\paragraph{Reference model dependency.}
12	The pipeline requires a fixed reference model; cross-architecture references degrade accuracy by 4--11\,pp (Appendix~\ref{app:ref_ablation}), and no principled selection criterion exists beyond empirical ablation.
13	Additional caveats (single LoRA seed with ${\sim}$1--3\,pp uncertainty, adversarial robustness, passage length sensitivity) are detailed in the Appendix.
14	
15	\section*{Ethics Statement}
16	
17	This work uses publicly available pretrained language models (Pythia-1.4B, OLMo-1B, GPT-2~XL) and Wikipedia text as seed data.
18	No human subjects were involved, no private or sensitive data were collected, and no new models were released.
19	Our method is intended to support data provenance and training-data auditing; we acknowledge that depth estimation tools could in principle be misused to circumvent content moderation, though such risks are shared with all detection-oriented research.
20	Code and data will be released upon acceptance.
21	AI assistants were used in an auxiliary role for coding support and language polishing.
22	All scientific decisions, experimental design, analysis, and core writing were conducted by the authors.
